jobs.occupation: Robotics Controls Engineer, Geartrain Manufacturing, Optimus (Techniker/in - Elektrotechnik (Automatisierungstechnik)/Bachelor Professional in Technik)
jobs.description:
What to Expect

Optimus geartrain manufacturing team is seeking a skilled and highly motivated, equipment control engineer with high precision equipment build experience within gearbox, electric motor or other industries focusing on rotating machinery design and manufacturing. We work with the cross-functional teams (Design, Quality, Production, Sustaining, Automation, and Supply Chain) throughout the entire lifecycle of a product (from initial design through prototype development and into full production) to develop volume manufacturable designs and processes that will produce gearboxes. The role of the equipment control engineer is to support establishing to world-class production line for gearboxes and drive scalable design and production methods used to make “the machines that make the machines”.  The ideal candidate takes pride in their work, has excellent engineering and physics fundamentals with hands on experience, is excited about manufacturing equipment and process development, does not shy away from a challenge, highly organized, has great attention to detail, and is able to work in fast paced development environment. with analytical and practical engineering focus.  

What You’ll Do

- Participate in initial equipment conceptual development, carefully balancing product specifications, process control requirements, layout complexity, cost, quality, and lead-time limits
- Implement control reliable safety systems (e.g., ANSI/RIA 15.06 and OSHA compliant) for safeguarding robots, gantries, conveyors, and other high-volume manufacturing equipment
- Architect, write, and debug PLC logic, emphasizing code organization, structure, documentation, maintainability, and reusability
- Architect, write, and debug programs for subsystems such as robots, vision systems, test equipment, and manufacturing execution systems
- Participate in Tesla specification and standard creation, release to vendors, and quote technical evaluation
- Select and size electrical and electromechanical components
- Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens for complex machinery, providing sufficient feedback for troubleshooting
- Lay out new industrial electrical control panels that are NFPA 79, NEC, and UL 508A compliant, and create electrical, pneumatic, and fluid schematics
- Manage electrical cabinet builds, field wiring, pneumatic, and fluid plumbing
- Introduce automated processes into production, and train maintenance and production teams to support after deployment into production

What You’ll Bring

- Proficiency in standard and safety PLC programming (e.g., Siemens TIA Portal, Allen Bradley Studio 5000, Beckhoff TwinCAT 3)
- Proficiency in script-based programming (e.g., Python, Go, SQL)
- Proficiency in robot programming (e.g., Fanuc, Kuka, ABB)
- Proficiency in servo system commissioning (e.g., Siemens SIMATIC, Rockwell Kinetix, Beckhoff Drive Manager 2)
- Proficiency in 2D/3D vision system programming (e.g., Keyence XGX, Cognex Insight, LMI Gocator)
- In-depth knowledge of equipment safety standards (e.g., ANSI/RIA 15.06, OSHA compliant) and electrical standards (e.g., NFPA 79, NEC, UL 508A)
- Degree in Mechatronics or related field, or equivalent experience
- Ability to communicate at a professional level in English language, both verbally and written
- Ability to travel internationally on a regular basis

Tesla is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer committed to diversity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

Tesla is also committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your recruiter know if you need an accommodation at any point during the interview process.

Privacy is a top priority for Tesla. We build it into our products and view it as an essential part of our business. To understand more about the data we collect and process as part of your application, please view our Tesla Talent Privacy Notice.

Apply at: https://www.tesla.com/careers/search/job/276897?source=BA

jobs.occupation: Lead Human Pharma Public & Government Afffairs (Obesity and Metabolic Health) (Leiter/in - Public Affairs (Lobbying))
jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com
The Position
As Lead Human Pharma Public & Government Affairs Obesity and Metabolic Health you will join a dynamic team dedicated to engaging with policymakers around the world to enable the access and uptake of life-changing pharmaceutical innovation. As part of the Public & Government Affairs function in the Corporate Affairs division, you will deliver integrated campaigns to drive meaningful policy change in particular areas of healthcare. At this time, we especially welcome applications from candidates with experience in policy shaping focused on Obesity and Metabolic Health, the therapeutic focus can shift in role based on business need.
This position is based at our Global Headquarters in Ingelheim, Germany.
Tasks & responsibilities

- As the Public & Government Affairs Lead for Obesity and Metabolic Health, in alignment with colleagues in the Corporate Affairs division, you will ensure we develop and implement integrated campaigns. In support of our established portfolio and future launches, you will establish alliances for awareness raising and targeted policy prioritization.
- One of your key tasks will be policy and stakeholder mapping to ensure the company has an informed position for key therapeutic areas within the Human Pharma business. You will lead on the creation of clear policy positions and support wider evidence generation to enable global and country teams to engage with policymakers.
- You will enable Public & Government Affairs capabilities and execution with a particular focus on the EU5, US, China and Japan.
- Moreover, you will support the Head of HP Public & Government Affairs to coach country teams in the development of clear strategic and tactical plans with measurable policy outcomes.
- You will be the main contact person for assigned Therapeutic Areas and other partners in the Human Pharma business. You will provide clear strategic counsel and be recognized as an expert in international health policy and country-level policy change.
- You will establish strong cross-functional relationships with teams including Communications, Market Access, Medical, Marketing, Legal and Compliance.

Requirements

- Master's degree in politics, Health Policy, Sciences, Economics, Law, or equivalent experience
- Several years of experience in a Public & Government Affairs role, potentially in-house, a consultancy or directly in Government
- Deep understanding of healthcare policymaking at a national and global level, including the role of the pharmaceutical sector in general and linked to specific therapeutic areas
- Business know-how to succeed in a global, matrixed organization, able to lead without direct management responsibility
- Demonstrable experience of delivering integrated campaigns to drive meaningful policy change
- Extensive experience in external networking to build meaningful relationships that drive (policy) change
- A true Thearapy Area policy leader with a co-creative mindset and the ability to build trust across the business
- Experience of ensuring successful delivery in line with the Legal and Compliance requirements in the pharmaceutical industry
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills with fluency in English (additional languages are a plus)

With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

Ready to contact us?
If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team, Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or via mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.com
Recruitment process:
Step 1: Online application - The job posting is presumably online until August 12th, 2026. We reserve the right to take the posting offline beforehand.
Step 2: Virtual meeting till mid August
Step 3: On-site interviews are planned for August 26th-28th
Please submit your application documents in English.

jobs.occupation: Operational Excellence Engineer (m/f/d) (Lean-Manager/in)
jobs.description:
Operational Excellence Engineer (m/f/d)

Shape the future of manufacturing at Kelvion in Herne as an Operational Excellence Engineer and drive real, measurable improvements across our operations. You will identify and implement optimization opportunities using Lean, Continuous Improvement, and Operational Excellence methods such as 5S, Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, Root Cause Analysis, and Gemba Walks. This is a high‑impact role where you directly influence efficiency, costs, and sustainability in a growing, technologically advanced industrial environment.

Your Role

- Lead Operational Excellence projects independently in close cooperation with all departments, including savings identification and cost analysis.
- Integrate improvements into daily operations with a strong shopfloor focus and ensure sustainable implementation.
- Moderate workshops and cross‑functional initiatives, and train and coach employees in OPX methods and tools.
- Perform value‑stream analyses, derive action plans, and report project progress, savings, and OPX successes.
- Collaborate across sites to create synergies and foster a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.

Attractive Offer & Environment

- Competitive salary package with attractive benefits, reflecting your expertise and contribution.
- Work in a growth‑oriented industry with strong demand for energy‑efficient and industrial solutions, offering long‑term job security and career development opportunities.
- Join a diverse, international team where different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences are valued. We are committed to an inclusive workplace and welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, nationality, or other personal characteristics.

Your Background

- Degree in Engineering, Business, Production Technology, or a comparable field.
- At least 3 years of experience in Lean, Continuous Improvement, or Operational Excellence in an industrial environment.
- Solid knowledge of Lean tools and methods (Six Sigma a plus); strong MS Office skills and basic ERP experience.
- Experience with tools such as MS Planner, Visio, Lucidchart, or Power BI is an advantage.
- Excellent communication skills in English and German, team‑oriented mindset, hands‑on attitude, and strong analytical and solution‑driven thinking.

Join Kelvion in Herne and help us build a more efficient, agile, and sustainable production environment on a global scale. We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Software Engineer (f/m/d) - Life Science and Diagnostics (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description:
Overview  

 
At QIAGEN, we are driven by a simple but powerful vision: making improvements in life possible.  

We’re dedicated to revolutionizing science and healthcare for the better. From our entrepreneurial roots to our current global presence, we've grown into a force for positive change. With thousands of employees across six continents, collaboration is our greatest strength. We’re always striving to identify talented individuals to join our exceptional teams. 
 
We have played a pivotal role in shaping modern science and healthcare, and we're just getting started. If you're someone who thrives on new challenges, values diversity and wants to make a tangible difference in people's lives, then QIAGEN is the place for you. 

 

At QIAGEN, every day is an opportunity to make a real-life impact. 

 

Join us, grow with us, and together, let's shape the future of biological discovery. 

‎

About this opportunity

In the position of a (Junior) Software Engineer (f/m/d) in Life Science and Diagnostics at QIAGEN, you will be making improvements in life possible – every working day. We are looking for you to help us shape our product development with skill and passion. You will work with our system and software teams to develop instrument control software for laboratory devices as well as data analysis software to process test results helping our customers to get valuable insights from a biological sample.

Your Tasks
* As a Software Engineer you will typically work in project teams of 5-10 people and gain experience in different roles throughout the life cycle of a software development project.
* You will start as a software developer or (automated) software tester in one of our scrum teams. Throught your professional career you will have the opportunity to grow into senior roles such as senior engineer, product owner, software architect or verification manager.  
* You will work across teams and across sites to generate the best possible solution for our products in a complex environment of Biology, Chemistry, Mechanics, Electronics and Software.
* You will be based at QIAGEN Hilden, our operational headquarter and will have the opportunity to visit our international development sites in Aarhus, Denmark or Wroclaw, Poland to strengthen and refine your software development capabilities.

Your Profile
* You have a master’s degree in computer science, with a minor in medicine, science or engineering
* You show a strong interest in software and product development and have already gained first professional experience.
* You love science and have a strong analytical mindset that strives to analyze, understand and solve problems.
* You are highly organized, work independently and easily adapt to changing work environment.
* You show excellent communication skills in both, English and German (C1 level)
* Ideally, you are familiar with working with AI-powered development tools or large language models to automate software development lifecycle processes. Experience with connecting AI agents with third-party systems using Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a plus

Please provide a transcript of record and an employer's reference if applicable.

What we offer  

 

* Bonus/Commission  

* Local benefits   

* Referral Program  

* Volunteer Day  

* Internal Academy (QIALearn)   

* Employee Assistance Program   

* Hybrid work (conditional to your role) 

 

Our people are the heartbeat of everything we do. Passion drives us as we push boundaries to innovate and evolve. We inspire with our leadership and make an impact with our actions. We cultivate a collaborative, supportive environment where each individual and team can flourish. We champion accountability and encourage entrepreneurial thinking.   

 

QIAGEN is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, or disability.

jobs.occupation: Engineer - CTO (m/f/d) (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description:
As the leading company in the field of software solutions for healthcare, we operate in 19 countries and employ over 9,000 dedicated staff members. You will work in a dynamic and innovative environment full of opportunities. With your commitment and passion, you have the chance to make a sustainable difference.

CGM Leverages AI: We’re looking for people who feel the power of AI in the e-health environment, who want to help shape change, and who are driven by a curious passion to see how technology can make healthcare smarter, simpler, and better.

Together, we are shaping the healthcare system of the future. Become part of our mission and make a difference - for a world where knowledge saves lives!

Are you passionate about groundbreaking products? Do you have the talent to turn ideas into real, valuable solutions-while always keeping the bigger picture in mind? Then we’d love to meet you!

You take end-to-end accountability for a large, distributed engineering organization that owns our ambulatory SaaS solutions and the shared framework modules used across all AIS DE products.

You co-define and drive the strategic product-technology roadmap for our cloud-based ambulatory portfolio in close collaboration with the executive leadership team.

You ensure that healthcare regulatory requirements-including medical device regulations, audits, and compliance-are rigorously embedded into product development, delivery, and operations.

You lead senior leaders and cross-functional teams, continuously increasing scalability, quality, AI maturity, and innovation velocity across products and platforms.

You represent the domain internally and externally, build strong executive-level stakeholder relationships, and position CGM as a leading SaaS provider in the Health-IT market.

Long-standing leadership experience at Director / VP / CTO level in SaaS product development, ideally with responsibility for large, distributed engineering organizations and complex product portfolios.

Exceptional academic background with a completed university degree and excellent grades, preferably in computer science, medical informatics, engineering, or a comparable technical field.

Deep expertise in cloud architectures and SaaS platforms, including modern DevOps practices and reliability engineering; hands-on experience with healthcare regulations (medical devices, audits, certifications) is a strong advantage.

Proven track record of driving AI adoption in engineering organizations, ideally with first-hand familiarity of Claude Code or comparable agentic coding tools (agents, skills, and workflows) and experience shaping AI pipelines, harnesses, and context engineering at organizational scale.

Excellent English and very good German, a strategic and entrepreneurial mindset, strong execution focus, outstanding leadership and communication skills, and the ability to guide complex organizations through transformation while staying clearly aligned with our healthcare purpose.

Mobile work: Work flexibly on the move two days a week and on site three days a week.

Attractive locations: In addition to fully equipped workplaces, regular events such as summer parties and Christmas parties await you at our locations.

Development: Our in-house academy and our portfolio of external cooperation partners will support you in your further development.

Health: Health is a valuable asset for us. Our in-house canteen offers a selection of tasty and healthy dishes every day, and we welcome you to our fully equipped fitness center for weekly courses (online & offline).

More is always possible: The kindergarten on our CGM campus in Koblenz helps our employees to organize their working day even more flexibly. We also offer corporate benefits, the option of a job bike, a company pension scheme, and much more.

Diversity is part of CGM! We look forward to receiving your application regardles...

Process Operator (f/m/d)

Place of work: Production site, near Chemnitz, Germany
Start date: ASAP
Contract type: Full-time

About us

We’re on a mission to revolutionize how the world produces protein and we’re just getting started.

Pacifico is a Leipzig-based biotech company producing the world’s most cost-competitive texturized protein through fermentation. Our technology makes sustainable, high-quality protein cheaper than conventional meat production – not just better for the planet, but better for you.

Our production site near Chemnitz is where science meets scale: industrial fermentation systems, food-grade processing lines, and a team that moves fast. We’re now looking for a Process Operator (f/m/d) to support the day-to-day facility operations at our production site.

The role

In this role, you will support the operations of our fermentation facility and all related processing steps. You will work closely with a Senior Process Lead and will be trained on our equipment, processes, and quality standards.

The role is strongly hands-on and operational, with a focus on running equipment, preparing materials, and supporting production. Working hours are initially within typical daytime working hours; as production scales, openness to late and occasional weekend shifts is valued.

Your main tasks

- Preparation of fermentation media (weighing, mixing, heating, handling raw materials)
- Operating fermentation tanks and auxiliary equipment
- Supporting downstream processing (emptying tanks, handling and processing biomass)
- Operating our food processing line and its associated equipment
- Monitoring basic process parameters (e.g. temperature, time, filling levels)
- Cleaning and sanitising equipment (CIP systems and manual cleaning)
- Maintaining cleanliness, order, and safety in the facility
- Documenting basic production activities and flagging issues when they arise

Your profile

- Practical experience in food & beverage or similar manufacturing environments
- Comfortable working in a production setting with physical tasks and machinery
- Careful, reliable, and quality-oriented working style
- Interest in food production and fermentation processes
- Ability to work well in a small team and communicate clearly on the shop floor
- Basic working knowledge of English

Nice to have

- Experience in a brewery, dairy or fermentation-based production
- Technical or vocational training in a relevant field
- Familiarity with hygiene standards and food safety practices
- Experience with CIP systems or industrial cleaning routines
- Basic working knowledge of German

What we offer

- A full-time role with clear responsibilities and growth opportunities
- 28 days of paid holiday per year
- Subsidy for the Germany Ticket (“Deutschland-Ticket”)
- Hands-on training and close collaboration with experienced colleagues

How to apply

A short CV/brief overview of your previous work experience is sufficient.
